content: The white delineator posts with thin black bands mean Rheinland-Pfalz, not Bavarian Forest.
Telugu script on signage means Telangana, not Delhi.
The specific density and composition of the roadside deciduous forest means Nizjnij Novgorod, not Moscow.
The yellow rectangular directional sign means Saxony, not Rheinland-Pfalz.
The specific yellow truck livery means Central Java, not West Java.
White dashed lane markings on a red-brown road surface mean Northern Territory, not Brasília.
The specific dark brown wooden utility pole shape means Languedoc-Roussillon, not Auvergne.
The specific style of the white edge line on the road shoulder means North Rhine-Westphalia, not Saxony.
A yellow center line on a paved road means Quebec, not Alaska.
Yellow center lines on a two-lane highway mean South Dakota, not Quebec.
Yellow metal railings mean Pomeranian Voivodeship, not Warsaw.
The flat, treeless steppe horizon means Volgograd, not Nizhny Novgorod.
Concrete block construction without plaster means Veracruz, not Dominican Republic.
Lush tropical green hills mean Parana, not South Dakota.
The specific combination of sandy soil and Scots pine density means Brandenburg, not Pomeranian Voivodeship.
The flat horizon and lack of rolling hills means Oklahoma, not North Carolina.
Black and white painted curb stones mean Roraima, not Veracruz.
Tamil script means Tamil Nadu, not Telangana.
The presence of dense ferns along the roadside means Limousin, not Brandenburg.
Flat coastal plains mean Schleswig-Holstein, not Saxony.
The presence of Telugu script on the storefronts means Telangana, not Hyderabad.
Cyrillic script on road signs means Tverskaya, not Pomeranian Voivodeship.
The presence of dense, low-lying tropical scrubland and humid greenery means Pernambuco, not Parana.
The red and white vertical banner means Shandong Sheng, not Beijing.
The blue street light poles mean Maharashtra, not Telangana.
